The ratio of silicon atoms in the photospheres of Star_1 and Star_2 can be determined from the given bracket abundances and solar reference values.

For Star_1:
- [Fe/H]_1 = 0 dex → (Fe/H)_1 = (Fe/H)_☉
- [Si/Fe]_1 = 0.3 dex → (Si/Fe)_1 = 10^0.3 × (Si/Fe)_☉
- Therefore, (Si/H)_1 = (Si/Fe)_1 × (Fe/H)_1 = 10^0.3 × (Si/H)_☉

For Star_2:
- [Mg/H]_2 = 0 dex → (Mg/H)_2 = (Mg/H)_☉
- [Mg/Si]_2 = 0.3 dex → (Mg/Si)_2 = 10^0.3 × (Mg/Si)_☉
- Therefore, (Si/H)_2 = (Mg/H)_2 / (Mg/Si)_2 = (Mg/H)_☉ / (10^0.3 × (Mg/Si)_☉) = 10^{-0.3} × (Si/H)_☉

The ratio of silicon abundances (by number relative to hydrogen) is:
(Si/H)_1 / (Si/H)_2 = 10^0.3 / 10^{-0.3} = 10^{0.6} ≈ 3.98

Assuming similar photospheric hydrogen number densities (as is typical for such comparisons), the ratio of silicon atoms per unit volume is ~3.9. The stellar masses provided are extraneous to this calculation.
